reveal.auditorReaction: You expected a score of 70, but your official Sherpas financial health score is 26—placing you in the CRITICAL band. That is a brutal 44-point difference. Here is why: you earn a fantastic $180,000 salary, but your plan currently has a negative net cash flow of -$8,336 this year! Between car payments, student loans, credit card balances, and renting, your money is leaking out faster than you realize. Planning a $550,000 home purchase in 2027 alongside retiring at 58 is currently a collision course.

discoveries.title: THE CASH FLOW CRACK
discoveries.explanation: Despite earning $180,000 gross, your annual outflows exceed inflows by $8,336 this year. You are burning liquid reserves rather than building the down payment required for 2027.
discoveries.whyItMatters: A $550,000 home requires at least $110,000 in down payment and closing costs, but your accessible cash is currently only $30,000 against a $46,530 emergency requirement.
discoveries.auditorRemark: A $180,000 salary that burns $8,336 a year is not wealth accumulation; it is high-speed lifestyle inflation. We need to plug the leak before you sign a mortgage.

discoveries.title: THE RETIREMENT COLLISION (AGE 85 CLIFF)
discoveries.explanation: Retiring at 58 means 33 years of retirement where guaranteed income covers only 34% of your spending needs. If you buy the $550k home in 2027 without restructuring, your liquid investments deplete at age 85 leaving unpaid living expenses.
discoveries.whyItMatters: The house and the age-58 retirement are actively cannibalizing each other in your financial plan.
discoveries.auditorRemark: You can have the house, or you can have retirement at 58 on your current track. Having both right now is financial fiction unless we fix your savings rate today.

discoveries.title: DEBT MULTIPLICATION
discoveries.source: Key Metrics — Debt Overview (Vehicle, Student, Amex)
discoveries.explanation: You are paying $950/month across a BMW 3 Series ($500/mo, $15k balance), Student Loan ($250/mo, $10k balance), and Amex Platinum ($200/mo, $3,500 balance at 20%).
discoveries.whyItMatters: That is $11,400 per year dedicated purely to debt service that could otherwise be funding your home down payment.
discoveries.auditorRemark: That BMW and Amex are costing you nearly a thousand dollars every single month. That is your future down payment driving down the highway.
